pairs.difference: A has orange leather-like plastic tones and brown-orange recesses. B pushes the whistle's side and openings toward vivid red, against a pale lemon background.
pairs.fix: Keep the whistle orange, with muted brown-orange inside the openings and along the round side; use a richer golden-yellow background.

pairs.difference: A's bell and tubing retain yellow-gold and muted gold tones, with a distinct red cord. B's tubing and bell interior become broadly orange-brown, reducing that color separation.
pairs.fix: Draw yellow-gold brass with muted golden reflections and brown-gold recesses; keep the hanging cord distinctly red.

pairs.difference: A's cup and saucer carry cool lavender tones and clear blue rims against coral-red surroundings. B has cream-pink porcelain and burgundy surroundings, pulling more of the card into related warm hues.
pairs.fix: Use white porcelain with cool lavender shaded areas, clear blue rims, and a coral-red background; avoid a pink cast across the cup and saucer.

pairs.difference: Both separate red apples, orange wicker, green-and-white cloth, and a purple background. A has more vivid orange wicker; B has more muted brown wicker and stronger green leaves. Both retain plausible local colors.

Both use orange-brown wood, subdued gray metal hoops, and cyan surroundings. A's wood is more orange; B includes more muted brown and cooler gray in the hoops. Neither shows a decisive palette mismatch.

A separates yellow bodywork from neutral silver bumpers and a cool gray road. B's shaded doors and road shift toward brown, while the bumper carries a lavender cast, giving the lower card a warmer palette.
pairs.fix: Keep the taxi yellow with muted golden shaded panels, neutral silver bumpers, and a cool gray asphalt road rather than brown pavement.

pairs.difference: A pairs a yellow-orange tent with fresh yellow-green grass and blue-green distant trees. B's large tent side turns ochre-brown, and the forest shifts toward muted olive and dark green, weakening the warm-cool separation.
pairs.fix: Keep the tent yellow-orange, including its shaded side; use fresh green grass and cooler blue-green distant trees instead of an olive cast.

pairs.difference: A's pot retains violet-gray metal tones against varied forest greens. B's pot becomes mostly neutral charcoal, while peach-orange ground and orange timber occupy more of the card.
pairs.fix: Give the iron pot muted violet-gray color in its shaded surfaces; use less orange ground and preserve varied cool forest greens.

pattern: Generated cards tend to spread orange, red, or brown into shaded surfaces and surroundings, or replace material-specific muted colors with a narrower palette. The lessons repeatedly show warmer cream computers, brighter blue cameras, and orange leather replacing cooler or more restrained local colors.
